# 4 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Reason Over Maternal Love

---

**1** What is even more admirable is how they encouraged one another toward death through their words of mutual strengthening.

**2** It was reason that had made them firm in their convictions, the law that had made them noble, and their love for one another that carried them forward.

**3** Their suffering and their steadfastness were so striking that even the tyrant and his guards were filled with wonder.

**4** Indeed, the very parents who had raised such children did not grieve at their deaths but rejoiced in their courage.

**5** The mothers who had nursed these brothers were not overcome with grief at their deaths.

**6** For all women devoted to virtue are strengthened by reason — as was the mother of these seven.

**7** When she saw them being tortured one by one, her love for her children did not weaken her resolve to see them die for the sake of the law.

**8** Instead, she watched each one die and counted it as a sight worthy of the deepest joy.

**9** For she loved the law more than she loved her own children.

**10** Her children were noble and obedient, and therefore she urged them on to the struggle.

**11** What was the source of such love for the law in this woman? It was her devotion to God.

**12** For reason devoted to God is able to master even maternal love when the service of God calls for it.

**13** Let no one suppose therefore that a woman is weaker in character or virtue. For a woman educated in the law proves to be in no way weaker than men.

**14** If we speak honestly, she proves to be stronger — she was not being tortured herself, but she was watching seven sons tortured and enduring it all.

**15** For when reason, driven by devotion to God, has taken control of the passions, it governs even a mother's love for her children.

**16** And surely, just as wise Abraham was willing to offer his son Isaac on the altar for God, and the father's hand was not stayed by compassion for the child,

**17** so too this mother, freely and without any compulsion, gave up her seven sons for the sake of God.

**18** Through reason she governed her passions and overcame the anguish of losing seven children.

**19** She proved by her faithfulness to God that reason is truly sovereign over the passions — even the most powerful ones.

**20** She is therefore greater than all noble athletes, for she wrestled against passion in the most intimate of all arenas — the arena of a mother's heart.

**21** How right that she should receive the crown of victory, the crown of imperishable life, for having conquered every passion through reason!
